title: PPE, Chemical Labels and Safety Data Sheets

content.overview: This lesson teaches learners to use supplied PPE requirements, labels, safety data sheets, and pesticide-worker restrictions without inventing their own controls or exceeding authorization.

vocabulary.definition: Personal protective equipment used to reduce exposure when other controls do not fully eliminate a hazard.
Safety Data Sheet containing standardized information about a hazardous chemical, including hazards and precautions.
A pesticide-related interval during which entry into a treated area may be restricted except under specified conditions.

sections.title: PPE follows the hazard and task
sections.body: PPE selection follows the employer's hazard assessment, work instruction, product label and applicable requirements. Workers inspect required PPE and report missing, damaged or unsuitable equipment rather than substituting based on preference.

sections.title: Use current chemical information
sections.body: Hazard Communication requires access to chemical hazard information. Technicians should locate product identity, hazard and precautionary statements, first-aid information, storage guidance and relevant PPE information in the supplied label and SDS. Agricultural pesticide restrictions may also control whether a worker may enter or perform a task.

workedExamples: A technician checks the current label and SDS before using a cleaning chemical instead of relying on memory from a different product.
A treated-area restriction conflicts with the task schedule, so entry is verified before work begins.
commonMistakes: Choosing PPE based only on comfort or habit.
Assuming cultivation training grants pesticide-handler authority.
content.practicalApplication: Use a mock label, SDS excerpt and work order to identify hazards, required supplied PPE, precautions and any condition that blocks the task.
content.summary: Chemical and PPE decisions are controlled by current product information, workplace procedures and applicable rules. Technician I learners must know how to find and follow those controls.

blocks.title: PPE is task-specific
blocks.body: Personal protective equipment is one layer of control. The workplace hazard assessment comes before PPE selection, and the required equipment can change with the task, chemical, work area, and applicable procedure. Inspect required PPE before use and report missing, damaged, contaminated, poorly fitting, or unsuitable equipment rather than substituting by habit.

blocks.alt: Diagram linking the assigned task, employer hazard assessment, product label and Safety Data Sheet, and applicable restrictions to the current SOP or work-order decision and required PPE.
blocks.caption: The PPE decision is made from controlled information for the actual task—not from memory or a generic rule.

blocks.title: Where the technician looks for controlled information
rows: Task sequence, site controls, required records, escalation path
Product identity, labeled use, precautions, required protections or restrictions
Hazards, first aid, handling/storage, exposure controls, spill information
Task hazards and selected PPE/control requirements
Whether entry or work is allowed and under what conditions

blocks.title: More PPE is not automatically better PPE
blocks.body: Adding unrequired equipment can create heat, visibility, dexterity, communication, or compatibility problems. Use the PPE selected for the assessed task and do not improvise respiratory protection or pesticide-handler status from a course certificate.

blocks.title: The schedule conflicts with a treated-area restriction
blocks.setting: A technician is assigned to move plants in a room treated earlier in the day. The move is on the task schedule, but a restricted-entry notice is still posted.
blocks.prompt: What is the correct next step?
options: Enter because the work order is already approved
Verify the current restriction and worker authorization before entry
Remove the notice because the plants need to move
Use extra gloves and enter for only a few minutes
blocks.answer: Verify the current restriction and worker authorization before entry.
blocks.feedback: A production schedule does not cancel a label-based or site-controlled entry restriction. The technician verifies current status and authorization before proceeding.

blocks.title: Mock label and SDS lookup
blocks.instructions: Using a supplied mock product label, SDS excerpt, and work order, locate the information needed to decide whether the task can proceed.
prompts: Identify the product and the assigned use.
Locate the primary hazard and precaution statements.
Identify the stated exposure controls or PPE information.
Find one storage or incompatibility warning.
Identify any restriction or missing information that should stop or escalate the task.

left.label: Controlled decision
left.body: The technician checks the exact product label, current SDS, task instruction, and site requirements before using the chemical.

right.label: Unsafe shortcut
right.body: The technician remembers how a similar product was used last month and assumes the same concentration, PPE, and entry conditions apply.

blocks.title: Key takeaway
blocks.body: Technician I competence means knowing where to find the controlling information, recognizing conflicts or missing information, and stopping to verify instead of inventing a chemical or PPE decision.
